properties.headline: Flood Advisory issued May 22 at 9:01PM CDT until May 23 at 1:00AM CDT by NWS Austin/San Antonio TX
properties.description:
* WHAT...Small stream flooding caused by excessive rainfall is
expected.

* WHERE...A portion of south central Texas, including the following
counties, Edwards, Kerr and Real.

* WHEN...Until 100 AM CDT.

* IMPACTS...Minor flooding in low-lying and poor drainage areas.
Rises in small streams and normally dry arroyos. Dangerous flows
over low-water crossings.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 859 PM CDT, Doppler radar indicated heavy rain due to
thunderstorms. This will cause small stream flooding. Up to 1
inch of rain has fallen.
- Additional rainfall amounts of 1 to 2 inches are expected
over the area. Since there has been several areas that have
already seen 1 to 2 inches of rain in the past two days, this
additional rain will result in minor flooding. Some larger
streams and rivers may be running at slightly elevated flows
and could rise a few feet from this extra rain.
- Some locations that will experience flooding include...
Kerr Wildlife Management Area, Lost Maples State Natural
Area, Vance, Mountain Home, Prade Ranch and Devil's Sinkhole
State Natural Area.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood

deaths occur in vehicles.

dangers of flooding.

killers in heavy rains. Campers and hikers should avoid streams or
creeks.

enforcement and to the National Weather Service in Duluth when you
can do so safely. Flooding can be reported to the National Weather
Service at 1-800-685-8612.

properties.areaDesc: Yap; Melekeok; Airai; Koror; Peleliu; Angaur
properties.headline: Special Weather Statement issued May 22 at 4:08PM ChST by NWS Tiyan GU
properties.description:
A tropical disturbance, known as JTWC's Invest 99W, is currently
centered near 7N147E west of Weno, Chuuk. This system is starting to
develop and is expected to move to the west-northwest as it moves
through the outer islands of Yap State. The chance of this system
developing into a significant tropical cyclone is rated as sub-low by
Joint Typhoon Warning Center (JTWC). Current estimations has the
system passing by or over Fais and Ulithi before moving northward
into the Philippine Sea. This system is expected to bring numerous to
widespread showers with possible heavy down pours, gusty winds and
choppy seas. In addition, high uncertainty remains regarding rainfall
amounts, but model trends indicate 3 to 5 inches over the next 72
hours. Yap Proper and Palau may also experience this disturbance as
models are not in alignment on when the northward turn is anticipated
to happen.

As of this writing, combined seas are expected to become choppier,
however remaining below 22 knot winds and 10 foot sea conditions.

Residents are urged to pay close attention the next few days to your
local emergency management, the National Weather Service Guam web
page (which can be found at www.weather.gov/gum), information put
out by Weather Service Offices Yap and Palau, and our social media
pages.

properties.headline: Hydrologic Outlook issued May 21 at 9:27PM AKDT by NWS Fairbanks AK
properties.description:
ESFAFG

...Locations Impacted...
Yukon Delta

As of Thursday evening, an Ice Jam near Russian Mission continues to
back up water from Russian Mission to Anvik. When the ice jam
eventually releases this water will flow towards the Yukon Delta.
Most large Yukon River ice jams during recent years decay, erode and
fail within a few days. The current jam at Russian Mission has been
in place for over 4 days. Water levels are expected to quickly rise
as the backwater makes its way downriver impacting communities like
Emmonak, Alakanuk, Nunam Iqua, and Kotlik.
